newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Newly-merged Adecco reports sales gain.
newsitem.headline: Newly-merged Adecco reports sales gain.

text.p: Newly-merged Swiss-French temporary employment giant Adecco SA reported group sales in its first year rose nine percent to 8.524 billion Swiss francs.
The comparable figure for 1995, before the firm was formed by merging Swiss concern Adecco SA and France's Ecco SA, was given at 7.830 billion Swiss francs.
The figure does not include divestitures of certain operations, including a cleaning business and a security division, and some acquisitions in the U.S. and Europe.
Sales for the fourth quarter alone, to December 29, 1996, were 2.257 billion. That compared with 1.869 billion in the 1995 period, making for a gain of 21 percent.

"In view of the challenging economic situation in France, Germany and Switzerland, we are satisfied with the overall development of Adecco," said Adecco's chief executive officer John Bowmer in a statement released with the company's results.
The company said it was confident that revenues in its main market, France would benefit from the merger, but also said the weak economy in France would continue to pose a challenge.
Christoph Gretler, equity analyst at CSFB in Zurich, said sales were above his expectations, due mainly to strength in European sales outside of France.
Adecco reported that sales in Europe excluding France rose 23 percent over the year, and 29 percent in the fourth quarter.
"Apart from business in France, business in the rest of Europe, with a gain in revenue of 29 percent, went exceedingly well," Adecco said.
Sales in France were virtually flat for the year, at 3.812 billion Swiss francs compared with 3.829 billion in 1995.
Gretler said France as a region would bear watching, noting that the market had been supported by the French government's economic subsidies.

"One has to see that certain impulses were given to the market by the state via tax reductions. That had a positive impact, but longer-term one will have to see if the market remains strong," he said.
He is forecasting 1996 net profit, before goodwill amortisation, at 265 million francs for the group, which would be roughly a gain of 10 percent, he said.
Adecco's shares on the Swiss exchange were up 2.00 Swiss francs, or 0.5 percent, at 427.00 in late morning trade after the results were announced. That was also two franc higher than the opening.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) was up 0.34 percent or 15.6 points at 4541.1.
